payload.title: Long-lived NATS subscribers (the four gateway WebSocket bridges and sensor-service's two request responders) call connect() once at boot and only log a failure, so a broker that is slow or away at that moment leaves them disconnected until the process restarts; most of them also inherit the factory's reconnect budget and stay closed after a long outage
evidence: apps/gateway-api/src/websocket/farm-nats-bridge.service.ts:205 (the failure is logged; nothing tries again, though the comment below says the status loop will)
apps/gateway-api/src/websocket/messaging-nats-bridge.service.ts:114 (one connect() at module init, failure logged at :123)
apps/gateway-api/src/websocket/nats-bridge.service.ts:130 (one connect() at module init, failure logged at :146)
apps/gateway-api/src/websocket/st-language-bridge.service.ts:126 (one connect() at module init, failure logged at :133)
apps/sensor-service/src/ingestion/sensor-lookup-responder.service.ts:278 (one connect() at module init; the warning says it waits for the next process restart)
apps/sensor-service/src/automation/compiler/nats-handlers/st-language.handler.ts:68 (one connect() at module init; the warning promises a retry on the next request that no code makes)
libs/backend-common/src/nats/nats-connection.factory.ts:264 (50 reconnect attempts by default; the four gateway bridges keep it, so a connected bridge closes for good after an outage of about 100 s)
payload.rule_violated: A component whose only job is to be subscribed recovers its subscriptions without a restart, whatever the broker's state at boot or during an outage
payload.notes: Seen in production on 2026-11-01: the gateway's farm bridge failed its first connect at 15:15:31Z, 19:01:24Z and 19:56:05Z (TLS handshake timed out while the gateway composed its supergraph) and stayed disconnected; live farm updates (batches, mortality, feeding, stock, site and tank changes) stopped reaching browsers. The other three bridges connected in the same boots.
